I learned to farm this land from my mother, watching her since I was a girl. Last season I put cow dung on this plot and the maize filled our bellies, so I will do the same this year. I do not have cash to buy chemical fertilizer from the cooperative — one bag is far too much for this small place, and I cannot risk borrowing when a bad season means hunger. I will plant the seed I saved from last harvest, pull the weeds with my own hands, and work this plot with my family for about twelve days over the season.
